verses.zh: 神啊，求你伸我的冤，向不虔诚的国为我辨屈；求你救我脱离诡诈不义的人。
verses.en: Vindicate me, O God!Fight for me[NOTE:1] against an ungodly nation.Deliver me[NOTE:2] from deceitful and evil men.[NOTE:3]
notes: Psalm 43. Many medieval Hebrew mss combine Psalm 43 and Psalm 42 into one psalm. Psalm 43 is the only psalm in Book 2 of the Psalter (Psalms 42-72) that does not have a heading, suggesting that it was originally the third and concluding section of Psalm 42. Ps 43:5 is identical to the refrain in Ps 42:11 and almost identical to the refrain in Ps 42:5.
Or “argue my case.”
The imperfect here expresses a request or wish. Note the imperatives in the first half of the verse. See also v. 3.
verses.commentary:
43:1 Because of

- the refrain in Ps. 42:5 and 11, which reoccurs in Ps. 43:5

- no introduction in the MT in Psalm 43 (the only Psalm in Book 2 with no introduction)

this was probably part of Psalm 42 at one time but was divided for some
unknown reason. The Jewish Study Bible's marginal note (p. 1330) suggests
that the fact that Psalm 42 focuses on the past, while Psalm 43 focuses on
the future, that may be a hint as to why and where they were divided!

▣ "vindicate" This VERB (BDB 1047, KB 1622, Qal
IMPERATIVE, cf. Ps. 7:8; 26:1; 35:24) basically means "to judge." The
psalmist is using court language (cf. Ps. 17:1-3). YHWH is the righteous and fair judge of all human
activity (i.e., Ps. 9:4).

▣ "plead my case" This is
also court imagery (BDB 936, KB 1224, Qal IMPERATIVE).
YHWH is the only fair and impartial judge! This same powerful court
imagery is in Romans 8:31-39!

▣ "an ungodly nation" If it
is true that Psalms 42 and 43 were originally one Psalm and that Ps. 42:6
means the author was in exile, then the "ungodly nation" would
probably refer to Syria.

It is surprising that the next line uses the descriptive phrase, "the
deceitful and unjust man!" One would have expected the PLURAL and a
description that focused on idolatry or aggression.

See Contextual Insights of Psalm 42, C.

▣ "from the deceitful and unjust man" Although this use of "man" is SINGULAR,
the synonymous parallelism that it is used in, is in a collective sense.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEBREW POETRY

verses.zh: 因为你是赐我力量的　神，为何丢弃我呢？我为何因仇敌的欺压时常哀痛呢？
verses.en: For you are the God who shelters me.[NOTE:1] Why do you reject me?[NOTE:2] Why must I walk around[NOTE:3] mourning[NOTE:4] because my enemies oppress me?
notes: Heb “from the deceitful and evil man.” The Hebrew text uses the singular form “man” in a collective sense, as the reference to a “nation” in the parallel line indicates.
Heb “God of my place of refuge,” that is, “God who is my place of refuge.” See Ps 31:4.
The question is similar to that of Ps 42:9, but זָנַח (zanakh, “reject”) is a stronger verb than שָׁכַח (shakhakh, “forget”).

The language is similar to that of Ps 42:9, but the Hitpael form of the verb הָלַךְ (halakh; as opposed to the Qal form in 42:9) expresses more forcefully the continuing nature of the psalmist’s distress.
verses.commentary:
43:2 Life is hard, unfair, and problems come
unexpectedly. All of us wonder why.

- have I offended God

- have I violated God's law

- is this a judgment for sin or a random occurrence of evil events and evil people in a fallen world?

The psalmist asks "Why" (Ps. 43:2), so do all humans!

Remember this is OT Wisdom Literature, which is a genre well known in the
ANE. It addresses questions all humans ask. For Israel, the questions are
related to YHWH and His revelations through Moses (i.e., the "Two Ways," cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28;
30:15,19; Psalm 1). The OT does not answer
all the questions in the same way as the NT. There is a change.

- progressive revelation

- new covenant

- the mystery of evil

SPECIAL TOPIC: SUFFERING

▣ "the God of my strength"
This is a recurrent refrain (BDB 731, i.e., a place of safety or
protection, often translated "refuge," cf. Ps. 27:1; 28:7-8;
31:2,4; 37:39; 52:7; Isa. 17:10; 25:4; 27:5; Jer. 16:19). Faithful
followers can always know that YHWH is their hope, protection, and place
of safety amidst the problems and conflicts of this fallen world. However,
this peace must be embraced. It is a faith act and a worldview that is
unrelated to the swirling circumstances of this present reality!

▣ "Why do I go mourning because of the
oppression of the enemy?" This is very similar to Ps. 42:9. The
question is, "who is the enemy?"

verses.zh: 求你发出你的亮光和真实，好引导我，带我到你的圣山，到你的居所！
verses.en: Reveal[NOTE:1] your light[NOTE:2] and your faithfulness.They will lead me;[NOTE:3] they will escort[NOTE:4] me back to your holy hill,[NOTE:5] and to the place where you live.[NOTE:6]
notes: Walk around mourning. See Ps 38:6 for a similar statement.
Heb “send.”
God’s deliverance is compared here to a light which will lead the psalmist back home to the Lord’s temple. Divine deliverance will in turn demonstrate the Lord’s faithfulness to his people.
Or “may they lead me.” The prefixed verbal forms here and in the next line may be taken as jussives.
Heb “bring.”
In this context the Lord’s holy hill is Zion/Jerusalem. See Isa 66:20; Joel 2:1; 3:17; Zech 8:3; Pss 2:6; 15:1; 48:1; 87:1; Dan 9:16.
verses.commentary:
43:3 "send" This VERB (BDB 1018, KB 1511, Qal
IMPERATIVE) is a prayer request which personifies YHWH's

- light ‒ BDB 21

- as YHWH's favor ‒ Ps. 4:6; 44:3

- as a guide ‒ Micah 7:8

- as eschatological light ‒ Isa. 9:2 (first coming of Jesus); Isa. 60:19-20 (second coming of Jesus)

- truth ‒ BDB 54 (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS IN THE OT)

- an attribute of YHWH often translated "faithfulness" ‒ Ps. 40:10; 71:22; 115:1; 138:2

- often personified as YHWH's agents or messengers ‒ Ps. 40:11; 43:3; 57:3; 85:10; 89:14

Notice what "the light" and "the truth" are to do.

- let them lead me ‒ BDB 634, KB 685, Hiphil IMPERFECT used in
a JUSSIVE sense

- let them bring me to Your holy hill ‒ BDB 97, KB 112, Hiphil IMPERFECT
used in a JUSSIVE sense

SPECIAL TOPIC: TRUTH

▣ "holy hill" This is one of
many ways to refer to the temple on Mt. Moriah in Jerusalem. It is also
called (usually with the ADJECTIVE "holy"):

- Zion (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: ZION)

- house

- sanctuary

- habitation

- temple

- mountain

- city of God

Here it is parallel to "Your dwelling places" (cf. Ps. 46:4;
84:1). The PLURAL denotes all the buildings of
the temple complex or the PLURAL OF MAJESTY
(cf. NIDOTE, vol. 2, p. 1132).

verses.zh: 我就走到　神的祭坛，到我最喜乐的　神那里。　神啊，我的　神，我要弹琴称赞你！
verses.en: Then I will go[NOTE:1] to the altar of God,to the God who gives me ecstatic joy,[NOTE:2] so that I may express my thanks to you,[NOTE:3] O God, my God, with a harp.
notes: Or “to your dwelling place[s].” The plural form of the noun may indicate degree or quality; this is the Lord’s special dwelling place (see Pss 46:4; 84:1; 132:5, 7).
The cohortative expresses the psalmist’s resolve. Prefixed with the vav (ו) conjunctive it also expresses the result or outcome of the preceding verbs “lead” and “escort.”

Heb “to God, the joy of my happiness.” The phrase “joy of my happiness” employs an appositional genitive. Synonyms are joined in a construct relationship to emphasize the degree of the psalmist’s joy. For a detailed discussion of the grammatical point with numerous examples, see Y. Avishur, “Pairs of Synonymous Words in the Construct State (and in Appositional Hendiadys) in Biblical Hebrew,” Semitics 2 (1971): 17-81.
verses.commentary:
43:4 The psalmist desires to go (BDB 97, KB
112, Qal COHORTATIVE) to the temple and
praise (BDB 392, KB 389, Hiphil IMPERFECT
used in a COHORTATIVE sense) God with his lyre
(BDB 490, i.e., a stringed instrument, cf Ps. 33:2). This is one more evidence
the psalmist is a Levitical musician.

▣ "God" The designation "God" appears four times in verse 4, but several
different forms.

- Elohim, line 1 and 4

- El, line 2

- Eloah. line 4

See
SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, A., C.

verses.zh: 我的心哪，你为何忧闷？为何在我里面烦躁？应当仰望　神，因我还要称赞他。他是我脸上的光荣（原文是帮助），是我的　神。
verses.en: Why are you depressed,[NOTE:1] O my soul?[NOTE:2] Why are you upset?[NOTE:3] Wait for God!For I will again give thanksto my God for his saving intervention.[NOTE:4]
notes: The cohortative with vav (ו) conjunctive probably indicates purpose (“so that”) or intention.
Heb “Why do you bow down?”
For poetic effect the psalmist addresses his soul, or inner self.
Heb “and why are you in turmoil upon me?”
verses.commentary:
43:5 This is the repeated refrain from Ps.
42:5,11. This is what unifies these two psalms.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS — see list at
Psalm 42. These two Psalms are a literary unit.

PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary which means
that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of
us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are
priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3).
Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above.
Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original
author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has
one and only one subject.
